title: Storage Redundancy and Replication
description: Choose between LRS, ZRS, GRS, and other redundancy options to protect your data from hardware failures and outages.

data.text: Azure Storage redundancy options determine how many copies of your data exist and where they are stored. Choosing the right redundancy level balances **durability**, **availability**, and **cost**. For most production data, you want copies that survive hardware failures and even entire datacenter outages.

Azure replicates your data synchronously within the primary datacenter or availability zone group. For geo-redundant options, it also replicates data asynchronously to a secondary region hundreds of miles away. If the primary region is unavailable, you can fail over to the secondary.

terms.definition: Three synchronous copies within a single datacenter. Lowest cost, lowest geographic protection.
Three synchronous copies across three availability zones in one region.
Six copies total: three in the primary region and three in a paired secondary region.
Like GRS, but the secondary region also allows read traffic for load balancing or DR.

data.title: Failover Is Manual by Default
data.text: Azure does not automatically fail over GRS accounts. You must initiate the failover yourself when you confirm the primary region is unavailable. Test your DR plan regularly.

data.title: Exercise: Compare Replication Options
data.description: Review the SKU matrix and choose redundancy for different scenarios.
steps: For each scenario below, choose a SKU and explain why:
a) A personal blog hosted on Azure Storage.
b) A financial records system requiring 16 nines durability.
c) A global e-commerce app that needs low-latency reads from any continent.
Write your choices and rationale in a short note.
data.expectedOutcome: A justified SKU choice for each scenario that balances cost, durability, and availability.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: LRS protects against hardware failures in one datacenter.
ZRS protects against datacenter failures within a region.
GRS and GZRS protect against regional outages by replicating to a secondary region.
Failover from secondary to primary is manual and must be planned.
data.takeaway: Redundancy is not optional for production data. Choose the right SKU based on your recovery objectives.
